analysis:
This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/ssd-maintenance-header-verdicts.md) and one modified table row in docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md (line 372, maintenance sweep). No executable source is supplied, so the underlying SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift change was not reviewed and cannot be verified here.

The docs describe a behavior change: maintenance now also runs after each write job. It caches readable DBK3 header verdicts keyed by lstat identity (device, inode, size, mtime, ctime). It re-parses only new, changed or unreadable files, and failed reads are never cached. It runs the directory checks once per fanout (fanoutPassesReadChecks) before reusing a cached verdict.

Relevant threat: T-041 (TB-007, A-001), which covers the SSD cache TTL, budget and ownership. The docs state that TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged, and the TTL stays 1800 s, so the T-041/SEC-035 sign-off bounds are not changed on paper.

Open questions for the code reviewer, none of them evidence of a regression from this batch:
1. An lstat-identity cache could in principle let a file with a forged or swapped header keep a stale ownership verdict if identity fields were reused or the clock were manipulated. A same-UID attacker could set mtime but not ctime, and ctime is included in the identity, which mitigates this.
2. Whether fanoutPassesReadChecks preserves the no-follow, regular-file, ACL and APFS-volume checks that the per-file read applies (CacheStorage.validateOpenedDirectory, SSDNoFollowIO), and whether a UUID mismatch or volume swap invalidates cached verdicts.
3. Whether files touched by a hit are re-parsed. The docs say they are, which keeps TTL sliding semantics correct.
4. Whether the cache is bounded in memory and pruned for deleted files.
5. Whether running maintenance after every write races with the write-in-progress lease and removalLock.

No findings are raised on documentation alone. needs_deeper_review is set because the implementing code was not supplied.
